answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from staking reputation bonds: each agent locks a deposit before it may transact, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove fraud or spam. One operator running many fake identities must fund every identity separately, so attack cost scales linearly with the number of fakes, while honest agents pay nothing beyond a temporary lock. Like ships paying harbor fees at a wharf, entry is cheap for one vessel but ruinous for a phantom fleet; a zephyr of free identities cannot overwhelm the market, and each violet credential stays tied to one bond.
